column7: LEVEL, DRIVE, TONE and DRY controls plus ADAPT and KLN/MOD/VOICE switching; proprietary Adaptive Circuitry changes the mid-forward voicing in response to guitar volume and playing dynamics; designed and built in England.
column10: The ADAPT control, KLN/MOD voice switch and DRY control are strong external/function identifiers. Preserve the 2023 introduction separately from later manual revisions or editions.

column7: JFET preamp with Drive plus Dry/Wet mixing, Tune, Shift, Range and Filter behavior; FM/AM radio-inspired signal destruction and a Tune CV input. Fairfield documents it as an FM modulator/demodulator and builds pedals in Hull, Quebec.
column10: The unusual radio-scramble control architecture and CV input make this a strong identification record. Do not reduce it to a generic fuzz/distortion label.

column7: Analog Morphing Core platform covers a broad clipping range from vintage velcro fuzz through more modern square-clipping textures; released and demonstrated by Kernom in 2023.
column10: Treat the Analog Morphing Core and digitally controlled morphing presentation as identification attributes while preserving the pedal as an analog-audio product rather than collapsing it into a generic digital multi-effect.

column7: Three-knob overdrive with builder-documented changes to mids, clipping character and low-end response relative to its reference family; introduced in 2023.
column10: Preserve 2023 introduction as the product identity anchor. Any later enclosure or production changes should be tracked separately from the original introduction.

column7: GPX documented a 2023 Fresh Fuzz 3K with Gain, Bite and Filter controls and a visible turret-board construction presentation, following an earlier two-knob Fresh Fuzz.
column10: Keep 3K as an edition/production variant lead until primary builder evidence establishes whether it is formally a generation.
